analysis: Examined the change in DistributedInstalledPairServingGrant.swift: publicTrafficLine (head ~lines 664-678) now defaults publicModels to ClusterPublicModels.current instead of .declared. It also computes declaredAssistant via ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant(runtimeModelID:artifactSHA256:in:) and passes tensorAssistant && declaredAssistant == nil to ClusterPairOwnerServing.publicTrafficLine. A constant string near head line 794 also changed (tensorAssistantNotOffered text). The patch excerpt was truncated, so that last hunk was not fully seen. The function only returns a descriptive UI/onboarding string. It is not an authorization decision: the doc comments state the coordinator's parity qualification and cluster approval still decide each public placement. The grant/refusal logic (grant, requireRank, plannable, startRefusal, admits) is unchanged in the visible hunks. The change is a display-only adjustment, so the tensor-assistant 'not offered' message is suppressed when the owner declared an assistant public for the artifact. The artifact binding is preserved: the assistant lookup requires a non-nil artifactSHA256 and is scoped by runtime model ID and artifact. No findings against the threat model (TB-007, TB-011, T-052, T-054) were identified in the supplied lines. Unverified integration questions: (1) the semantics of ClusterPublicModels.current versus .declared and ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant (not supplied); (2) whether the line suppression is mirrored by an actual enforcement path, such as ClusterConfiguration.validate and tensorAssistantServesLocally, so that a setup offered to the coordinator with the assistant is really covered by qualification; (3) whether this string drives any gating rather than display only. Those live in unchanged or unsupplied files, so a cautious flag for the next pass is warranted.
